To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antigen binding characteristics of IgG anti-CK18 antibodies in non-allergic asthma patients are heterogeneous.

1) the IgG autoantbodies to CK18 from patients with non-allergic asthma seem to preferentially bind the whole molecule of the CK18 protein, 2) the IgG antibody binding characteristics were heterogeneous among patients, and 3) the binding capacity of IgGs to N-terminal fragments of CK18 was decreased in two out of three patients.
the binding of IgG auto-antibodies to fragments of CK18, cleaved by cas-pase-3, was heterogeneous among the patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the antigen-binding characteristics and the pathophysiological roles of autoantibodies in nonallergic airway disease.
a novel mechanism of nonallergic asthma that is related to the autoantibody-mediated apoptosis of bronchial epithelia.
the antigen-binding characteristics and epitopes of IgG auto-antibodies to cytokeratin 18 protein in patients with nonallergie asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antigen-binding characteristics were different in patients with nonallergenic asthma and that these differences could be related to the different pathogenesis and/or severity of asthma.
there is no evidence to support the existence of an autoimmune mechanism in the pathogenesis of nonallergic asthma.
IgG autoantbodies to CK18 in nonallergic asthmatics bind to the intact CK18 protein and the epitope is not exposed in the cleaved form of the protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CK18 protein is an autoantigen associated in nonallergic patients with asthma.
IgG autoantbodies to CK18 in nonallergic asthmatic patients may be a useful biomarker of epithelial injury in asthma.

the IgG autoantbodies to CK18 in patients with nonallergie asthma may bind to the whole CK18 molecule and the binding capacity of the IgG autoabntibodies to CK 18 was heterogeneous among the patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IgG autoantbodies to CK18 in nonallergic asthmatics preferentially bind to N-terminal fragment and whole molecule of CK 18 protein.
the antigen binding characteristics of IgG antibodies to CK18 protein were different between patients and healthy controls.
the antigen-binding characteristics were not uniform in nonallergic patients with asthma.
